items.title: @haofeiyu44：How to build sample-efficient RL algorithms for long-horizon language agents? Our answer: Just ONE additional loss on to
items.abstract_or_text: How to build sample-efficient RL algorithms for long-horizon language agents? Our answer: Just ONE additional loss on top of GRPO can achieve up to 2× sample efficiency across 5 long-horizon agent benchmarks! By adding a multi-step action forecasting loss, we encourage the agent to learn action chunks from successful rollouts.

items.title: @levie：It's incredible to have reached a threshold where it's practical that AI will be better at training models than humans a
items.abstract_or_text: It's incredible to have reached a threshold where it's practical that AI will be better at training models than humans are so quickly. One day recursive self improvement feels far off, and the next we already have signs of what it will look like. Model capability finally exceeding most human engineers, advancements in the harness and infra for long running agents, a growing array of data, and the ability to parallelize the agents to work on vastly more tasks and tests and approaches than any person could have before, creates an incredible flywheel.

items.abstract_or_text: And @AIatMeta went live with Muse Spark Open! The 816B model was trained on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Its 1M-token context window gives coding agents room to work across large codebases. Meta also produced NVFP4 checkpoints optimized for Blackwell Ultra, delivering over 50K tokens/sec/GPU to improve throughput and lower cost per token.

items.title: @pushmeet：At @GoogleDeepMind, we believe one of AI's most transformative impacts is empowering scientists to solve society's harde
items.abstract_or_text: At @GoogleDeepMind, we believe one of AI's most transformative impacts is empowering scientists to solve society's hardest problems. Over the past year, we've evolved our coding agent, @Google @Antigravity, to accelerate end-to-end scientific workflows combining our latest Gemini models with science-specific: • breakthrough models like AlphaFold and AlphaGenome • new interfaces like the Biomolecular Structure Viewer The impact of this integration has been transformative for the pace of our research. As an example, in a single session using Antigravity, our researchers working on antimicrobial resistance surfaced a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate.

items.abstract_or_text: Working out how best to use AI in mathematics research—and in science more generally—will take time, effort, and resources. We're eager to support mathematicians as they drive scientific progress and define the future of their field. We've committed 5 million of funding, compute, and Claude access to help the math community navigate the massive changes that AI brings. We're partnering with @SimonsFdn, who will manage the award through a community-driven approach, supporting workshops, conferences, and lectures by domain experts.

Academic research starts with questions whose impact may take years to impact human health.

items.abstract_or_text: GPT-Rosalind is built to support that work: helping researchers reason across scientific literature and biological data, with scientists bringing the expertise and judgment to evaluate the evidence. Eligible labs can receive up to 12 months of sponsored access to OpenAI tools, with GPT-Rosalind access subject to trusted-access approval. Research data shared through the Rosalind Academic Plan is not used to train our models by default.

items.title: @AnimaAnandkumar：The importance of tipping points has been extensively studied, including in a recent @UN @ScienceBoard_UN brief for clim
items.abstract_or_text: The importance of tipping points has been extensively studied, including in a recent @UN @ScienceBoard_UN brief for climate modeling. But it is challenging to detect tipping points before they happen since they can appear suddenly. We address this in our latest paper appearing in @PNASNews Our recurrent neural operator tracks the history of changes and can predict the probability of tipping points happening in future and when it is likely to occur. The RNO was able to look more than two years ahead of the expected tipping point in the simulated data and predict its timing with an error of about 11 days.

items.title: @PlasmaAI：@OpenAI recently released a proof of the quasi-Riemann Hypothesis, which says there is some fixed θ < 1 such that no zer
items.abstract_or_text: @OpenAI recently released a proof of the quasi-Riemann Hypothesis, which says there is some fixed θ < 1 such that no zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part greater than θ. They prove it with θ = 7/8. The paper hasn't been peer reviewed yet, but its main theorem has a computer-checked proof in Lean. This improves the bound on the root-mean-square error of the prime count against li(N).
